articles.title: Who should Dodgers root for in NL wild card series? Breaking down Phillies, Braves matchups
articles.summary: The Dodgers await the winner of Game 3 between the Braves and Phillies. Who should they be rooting for?
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts sat back on the sofa in his office on Monday, looking the most relaxed he has in weeks.

He'll be leading the charge as the Dodgers try for a historic World Series three-peat starting Saturday. If the Dodgers succeed, they would be the first team in National League history to accomplish the feat. But that's not what's on Roberts' mind right now; he knows the danger of looking too far ahead once you're in October.

"It just makes life more difficult when you don't focus on the job," he said over Zoom. "And that's winning this next series."

Max Muncy echoed his skipper, adding that the team doesn't need to add any extra pressure. Instead, the Dodgers are focusing on staying sharp over the week off, coming in to workout at Dodger Stadium, take batting practice, throwing bullpens and watching the wild card games together.

The bye helps the Dodgers get healthier, too; both Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman have been using the time to work on their mechanics at the plate while managing knee ailments (and a right bicep injury for Ohtani).

It also helps the team to lock in by just being around each other.

"Winning the World Series is hard enough as it is," Muncy said. "So for us, we're just trying to focus on what we have ahead of us without the added noise to it."

What lies ahead for the Dodgers in the NLDS is still unknown. As the No. 2 seed in the NL, they'll face either the Atlanta Braves or Philadelphia Phillies , who have battled through two chaotic games so far ; the Braves jumped out to a 1-0 lead on Austin Riley's clutch three-run homer in the bottom of the eighth on Monday and led 3-1 late on Wednesday until back-to-back blasts from Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper tied it up. Alec Bohm then went deep on a solo shot in the 10th to force a decisive Game 3 on Thursday.

That means the Dodgers won't know who they play until the last possible minute. Not that they necessarily care who occupies the dugout across from them, anyway.

"Either team, it doesn't really matter," Muncy said. "You're gonna have to play nothing but good teams from here on out. It's the postseason ... any team can go out and beat you. ... Whoever we play is whoever we play."

Here's a look at each of the Dodgers' possible NLDS opponents:

2026 MLB playoffs open with thrilling wild-card series matchups

The Dodgers and Braves dueled in both the 2020 and 2021 NLCS, but just four players remain from that 2021 Braves team that won the World Series: Ozzie Albies , Austin Riley , Dylan Lee and Ronald Acuña Jr. The Dodgers have had plenty of turnover, too.

The biggest knock on this Braves team has been the pitching depth. Chris Sale is continuing to beat Father Time and has a solid argument against Jacob Misiorowski for the Cy Young Award, but there's a dropoff in the rotation after him. Tyler Mahle has pitched well since being acquired at the trade deadline with a 1.99 ERA in nine starts. He threw seven innings of one-run ball in Game 2 against Philadelphia, but he was also the only starting pitcher that president of baseball operations Alex Anthopoulos traded for this summer when the consensus around league circles was that the Braves needed at least another arm.

Atlanta's battled through injuries for most of the season but much like the Dodgers, the Braves seem to be getting healthy at the right time.

This would be a rematch of last year's NLDS, with home field advantage flipped to LA. The Dodgers are fully familiar with how dangerous the Phillies' lineup, headlined by Schwarber and Harper, can be; but they're just as familiar with how vulnerable the Phillies' bullpen is in October.

And the Phillies may have showed that volatility a little early with a 10-14 September record in which they didn't secure their playoff spot until the final game of the season despite their magic number being at one for the seven games before that. They avoided a historic collapse to close out the regular season and came back from what looked like sure elimination late in Game 2 on Wednesday, but how much longer can their bats keep covering for the bullpen? If it's anything like it was in 2025, the answer is not much.

articles.title: WNBA commentator Sydney Colson physically restrained after going after Fever fan following A'ja Wilson mess
articles.summary: Video footage captures Sydney Colson lunging at a spectator as an Amazon staffer physically restrains her during a WNBA playoff game Tuesday.
articles.body: Former Indiana Fever player and Amazon Prime commentator Sydney Colson lost complete control during Tuesday’s WNBA playoff game between the Las Vegas Aces and Fever, lunging at a spectator while a staff member physically restrained her. The chaos began when Aces star A’ja Wilson overreacted to a fan who simply pointed at her and shouted, "It’s on you!" following a foul call. Wilson marched two rows deep into the baseline seats to confront him, earning a technical foul for unsportsmanlike conduct. Instead of maintaining professional distance as a credentialed media member, Colson and fellow Amazon analyst Theresa Plaisance (also a podcast co-host with Wilson) left their courtside seats and inserted themselves into the altercation. As arena personnel escorted Colson and Plaisance away from the baseline, a spectator in a red Fever shirt directed a comment toward them. Plaisance pointed back and called him a "little b***h boy." Colson then continued pushing aggressively toward the fan as an Amazon staffer struggled to hold her back. Video footage captured her shouting, "Who do you think you are? B—-, who the f— do you think you are?" Colson spent the 2025 season in Indiana before exiting the franchise. Ever since packing her bags, taking public cheap shots at her former team has become a habit. Right on script, the broadcast team immediately scrambled to run cover for Wilson. Prime Video analyst LaChina Robinson insisted on-air that "something was said" simply because Wilson does not normally react that way. Aces coach Becky Hammon predictably chimed in, claiming she had never seen Wilson react like that and assuming her star felt "deeply disrespected." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Wilson doubled down after the game, apologizing to her teammates for picking up the technical foul while insisting the fan’s conduct crossed the line. "I don’t know if you guys know me, but I don’t get into the bulls—," Wilson told reporters. "I try to play my game, keep it pushing. But if I’m just walking, because I just got the foul, I’m chilling, and if I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don’t give a damn what you said. I don’t give a damn how you said it. The tone, that is unacceptable." Wilson went further, complaining about how the fan was allowed to return to his seat after security reviewed the incident. "And how he gets back in the game because they said he didn’t do anything? Of course he did, and that’s fine," she said. The Fever confirmed that arena security interviewed witnesses and found zero violations of the Fan Code of Conduct. In August, after Chicago’s DiJonai Carrington was ejected for a dangerous neck hit on Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, Colson publicly targeted her former teammate by sarcastically posting, "Love a trans foul," on social media. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In any other professional sports league, a credentialed commentator physically restrained from charging a paying fan would face immediate suspension or termination. Yet Colson remained mic’d up for Amazon’s broadcast during the entire outburst, while the live coverage rushed to defend Wilson without acknowledging that the fan broke zero rules. Don’t hold your breath waiting for Amazon or WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert to do anything about it. Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

articles.title: What Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz said about Ohio State before the game
articles.summary: Ohio State travels to Iowa for a Big Ten matchup Saturday. Watch and listen to what Hawkeye coach Kirk Ferentz said about the Buckeyes ahead of time.
articles.body:
As the season goes on, games tend to take on more importance at a place like Ohio State , and so it is this Saturday when the Buckeyes travel to Iowa City to take on a ranked Hawkeyes team. To make matters even more intriguing, Iowa just beat rival Michigan on a last-second play and are flying high heading into the matchup.

But Iowa head coach Kirk Ferentz knows last week was last week, and there's probably a bigger challenge ahead with a top-five Ohio State team coming to Kinnick for a game that will probably go a long way in deciding what happens in the Big Ten .

Ferentz met with the media in Iowa City earlier this week to reflect on the win over the Wolverines and to preview what's ahead with Ohio State. He was rather stoic in his assessment of the challenge it will be to play the Buckeyes, praising the talent, coaching, and size, and we've got all of his comments for you to watch and read here ahead of the game.

The Iowa head man talked at length about receiver Jeremiah Smith , the respect he has for Ryan Day , compared the Buckeyes to the Wolverines, and more.

Ohio State and Iowa are scheduled to kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. ESPN's College GameDay will be in attendance to make things even more fun. We'll have coverage before, during, and after, as always.

Contact/Follow us @BuckeyesWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Ohio State news, notes, and opinion. Follow Phil Harrison on X.

articles.title: FSU vs. Virginia: How to watch, stream, odds
articles.summary: The Seminoles welcome Virginia to Doak for the first time since 2014.
articles.body:
Florida State (2-2, 0-1 ACC) will look to get its win-loss record (in the ACC back to even this Saturday, taking on the Virginia Cavaliers (3-1, 1-0 ACC) in Tallahassee for the first time since 2014.

The Cavaliers are coming off a dominant 42-3 win over the Delaware Blue Hens. Virginia is currently favored by 2.5 points, according to FanDuel , with the over/under at 51.5.

The Cavaliers, who upset the Seminoles 46-38 in overtime last season, have won two straight and three of the last four in the series. FSU leads the all-time series 15-5, including a 9-1 home record.

Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2.

Florida State Seminoles vs. Virginia Cavaliers: How to watch, stream, odds

After two non-conference games, Florida State begins a stretch of seven straight ACC games by hosting Virginia on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. The game will air on ESPN2.

The Seminoles are 15-5 all-time against the Cavaliers, including a 9-1 record inside Doak Campbell Stadium. The last time FSU hosted Virginia, in 2014, Florida State won 34-20.

Quarterback Ashton Daniels is 58-of-97 passing for 928 yards and six touchdowns, with 142 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns. He has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all four games.

At No. 10 Alabama on Sept. 19, Daniels was 17-of-29 passing for 377 yards and two touchdowns, while rushing 13 times for seven total yards and two touchdowns. Daniels became the third Seminole in program history , joining Jordan Travis and EJ Manuel , with two rushing touchdowns and two receiving touchdowns in a game. Daniels' 377 passing yards were the most for a Seminole since 2022.

Daniels is the only player in FBS in 2026 with multiple rushing and passing touchdowns and a two-point conversion. He is one of just three players since 1995 to have touched the numbers in a road game against a Power 4 opponent.

Daniels has completed just 17 completions to rack up 377 yards. His 22.2 yards per completion are the most Alabama has allowed to a player with at least seven completions since 1995. Florida State scored 36 points at Alabama, the most the Crimson Tide have allowed in a non-conference game in Tuscaloosa since 2000.

articles.title: Eagles Injury Report: DeVonta Smith among 6 players listed under did not practice
articles.summary: The latest news and updates ahead of Week 4.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first official injury report of the week on Wednesday in advance of their Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams .

Note that this report is an estimation because the team held a walkthrough in lieu of a normal practice.

The Eagles listed six players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: DeVonta Smith , Zack Baun , Dallas Goedert , Will Shipley , Hollywood Brown , and Fred Johnson .

Smith did not practice on Thursday last week before ramping up to limited on Friday and full go on Saturday before playing against the Chicago Bears . Perhaps he'll follow a similar path this week as the Eagles look to manage his hamstring injury. If Smith can't play, well, that's a big problem.

Baun is a new addition to the report with a concussion. He'll have to be cleared before he can return to the field. If Baun can't suit up, look for Jeremiah Trotter Jr. to start in his place.

Goedert was always expected to miss multiple games, so, the Eagles will probably be without their top tight end again this weekend. Perhaps we'll see Zach Ertz's playing time increase in his second game back with the Birds.

Shipley is dealing with a foot injury that caused him to miss last Thursday's practice before being limited on Friday and Saturday. He was able to play against the Bears. We'll see if he's able to ramp up in practice over the next two days.

Brown and Johnson were unexpectedly added to the injury report after apparently getting banged up in practice last week. Until they return, one must assume they might not be able to suit up.

The Eagles listed three players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Moro Ojomo , Jordan Davis , and Jihaad Campbell .

All three players are new additions to the report.

Ojomo is listed with calf and elbow injuries.

Being listed as limited is better than being listed under DNP. These guys might be able to play against the Rams.

The Eagles listed five players under FULL PARTICIPATION: Jonathan Greenard , Jalen Carter , Darius Cooper , Tank Bigsby , and Byron Young .

Good to see Greenard was full go once again, just like he was on Saturday before playing on Monday. The Eagles need him to be able to handle a bigger workload … and soon.

Carter's injury is limiting his ability to function normally and handle his usual workload.

Bigsby missed some practice time last week with an abdomen injury.

Young is a new addition to the report with a toe injury.

PHILADELPHIA EAGLES INJURY REPORT (WEDNESDAY)

LB Zack Baun (concussion) WR Hollywood Brown (ankle) TE Dallas Goedert (knee) OT Fred Johnson (knee) RB Will Shipley (foot) WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring)

LB Jihaad Campbell (knee) DT Jordan Davis (calf) DT Moro Ojomo (calf/elbow)

RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) DT Jalen Carter (wrist) WR Darius Cooper (knee) EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) DT Byron Young (toe)

LOS ANGELES RAMS INJURY REPORT (WEDNESDAY)

The big news is that Sean McVay said he expects Puka Nacua will return to the field against the Eagles. Nacua hasn't played since getting banged up in Week 1.

The Rams' full injury report is yet to be announced — check back for updates.

articles.title: Yankees win Wildcard Game 1, could advance with win
articles.summary: BRONX, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) – The Yankees have the opportunity to advance to the next round of the playoffs on Sept. 30, taking game one from the Red Sox on Sept...
articles.body:
BRONX, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) – The Yankees have the opportunity to advance to the next round of the playoffs on Sept. 30, taking game one from the Red Sox on Sept. 29, 9-0.

The Yanks were led by the bat of Ben Rice , as he blasted two homeruns - one a solo shot and the other a grand slam. Cam Schlittler had a great night on the mound, going for 6.1 innings and striking out ten batters.

On Sept. 30, Max Fried will be taking the mound for New York with Sonny Gray pitching for Boston . Because the Wildcard round is a best of three series, if the Yankees win they will advance to the ALDS. The winner of the series between the Yanks and Red Sox will face another AL East rival in the Tampa Bay Rays .

First pitch is set for 8pm and you can tune in on NBC.

articles.title: Donald Trump responds after U.S. captain credits him for Presidents Cup victory
articles.summary: Donald Trump responds after Brandt Snedeker credits him for Team USA’s dramatic 17-13 Presidents Cup comeback at Medinah.
articles.body:
The United States turned a three-point Presidents Cup deficit into its 11th straight title at Medinah Country Club on Sunday. Brandt Snedeker's team trailed 10.5-7.5 before 12 singles matches began. The Americans then produced the biggest final-day comeback in Presidents Cup history, winning 9.5 of 12 points.

Jacob Bridgeman clinched the 17-13 victory with a 1-up win over Min Woo Lee. President Donald Trump attended the event as the honorary chairman and spoke with Snedeker before the matches. Afterward, Snedeker credited Trump with bringing energy to the team. Trump later praised the U.S. team for the turnaround.

Snedeker gave Trump a post-match shoutout

Snedeker made the Trump reference during his post-match remarks after the Americans completed their comeback. The U.S. captain said Trump had told him before the singles session that he was going to bring energy because the team needed it.

Snedeker then connected that conversation to a promise he had made before the round. He said that if the Americans completed the comeback, Trump would get the credit, adding a direct thank-you to the president.

The comments came after Snedeker had accepted responsibility for some U.S. struggles. The Americans had been outplayed in several team sessions, and Snedeker acknowledged Saturday that he had not handled all of his decisions as well as he wanted.

Trump watched the Americans erase the deficit

Trump arrived at Medinah before the 12 singles matches and greeted players and caddies from both teams on the first tee. He served as honorary chairman, a role he previously held at the 2017 Presidents Cup, when the United States also won.

Trump kept his remarks at the opening of the singles session short. A media outlet reported that he told the crowd, " These people want to see golf ," before turning his attention to the competition.

The visit came with the United States facing an unusual position in the event. The International Team had taken a 10.5-7.5 lead, the first time the Americans had entered the final singles session trailing on home soil, and the visitors were seeking their first Presidents Cup victory since 1998.

The U.S. singles performance changed everything

The Americans quickly attacked the deficit, with Cameron Young and Justin Thomas delivering early points. Scottie Scheffler, Chris Gotterup, and other U.S. players followed with wins that shifted the scoreboard in the home team's favor.

Two important swings came from Collin Morikawa and Jackson Koivun. Morikawa rallied against Hideki Matsuyama, while 21-year-old rookie Koivun made a late surge against Si Woo Kim that helped keep the American charge moving.

Patrick Cantlay also produced a major moment against Adam Scott, holing a birdie putt from roughly 57 feet on the 16th hole. Bridgeman then supplied the clincher, making a short par putt at the 18th to defeat Min Woo Lee and secure the 17-13 result.

The singles session ultimately turned a difficult opening position into a dramatic finish for the United States. The Americans collected enough points across the afternoon to erase the International team's advantage, with the late matches providing the final push toward the overall victory.

Fun fact: Medinah's Course No. 3 also hosted the 2012 Ryder Cup, where Europe erased a four-point deficit on Sunday to win 14.5-13.5, creating the famous "Miracle at Medinah" comeback.

After the victory, Trump described the comeback in strong terms while speaking to reporters after returning to Joint Base Andrews. AP reported that he said the U.S. team played "unbelievable golf" after entering the final day with a large deficit and coming out with a "tremendous victory."

His comments came after Snedeker had publicly credited Trump's presence and encouragement before the final session. Snedeker said Trump told him he would "bring some energy" for the team, and the captain later thanked the president after the U.S. victory.

The response did not change the competitive record that produced the trophy. The U.S. players won nine of the 12 singles matches, tied one, and lost two, turning the 10.5-7.5 deficit into a four-point final margin.

Snedeker's victory followed a difficult week

The final-day result reshaped the conversation around Snedeker's captaincy. On Saturday night, with the Americans three points behind, he said he did not think he had "held up" his end of the bargain and accepted responsibility for lineup and matchup decisions.

Sunday produced a different scene. Snedeker watched his players deliver the largest final-day comeback in Presidents Cup history, and Bridgeman's clinching putt ended the International Team's hopes of winning its first title since 1998.

The victory moved the United States' all-time Presidents Cup record to 14-1-1. It also extended an American winning streak that began in 2005, while the 2026 comeback added another chapter to Medinah's history of high-profile team-golf reversals.

The Presidents Cup stays in American hands

The 17-13 score completed a tournament that swung repeatedly at Medinah. The United States won the opening fourball session 3-2, the Internationals answered with a 5-0 foursomes sweep, and the visitors remained ahead entering Sunday.

The Americans' final-day surge made the closing score look comfortable, but the route there was anything but straightforward. Snedeker's team entered Sunday needing a major singles response, and the players delivered it by winning 9.5 of the 12 available points.

Trump's presence became part of the final-day story because of his role as honorary chairman and his interaction with the U.S. team. Snedeker's decision to credit him added another notable moment to a comeback ultimately decided by the players' performances across 12 singles matches.

The United States beat the International Team 17-13 at Medinah to win its 11th straight Presidents Cup.

Brandt Snedeker credited Donald Trump for bringing energy to the team before Sunday's singles matches.

Trump later praised the comeback and said the U.S. team played "unbelievable golf."

The Americans erased a 10.5-7.5 deficit by winning 9.5 of 12 singles points.

Jacob Bridgeman clinched the title with a 1-up victory over Min Woo Lee.

articles.title: Denver Broncos QB Bo Nix doesn’t put pressure on himself over slow starts
articles.summary: The question that is making the rounds this week about the Denver Broncos have been centered around their slow starts in games. Mostly that question has been...
articles.body:
The question that is making the rounds this week about the Denver Broncos have been centered around their slow starts in games. Mostly that question has been directed at head coach Sean Payton, but quarterback Bo Nix got hit with one today as well when he was asked if he puts any added pressure on himself to get faster starts going.

"Not really," Nix said on Wednesday . "Honestly, it can lead to a couple plays I did the other day, pressing, and you just make it worse. My job is just get the ball where it's supposed to get to, not force anything, take what the defense is giving me."

It was a good answer and entirely true. The last thing we want Nix doing is trying to force things. He's done a little of that here and there and the results haven't been great. Nix can create plays on his own, but that is more instinctual football than it is intentionally forcing things. No, early in games we just need to see the offense execute better on early downs and get ahead of the sticks. They do that well in the second half, but for whatever reason suck at it in the first half.

The Denver Broncos safety played a big role in their comeback victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3.

Talanoa Hufanga and the Broncos just pulled the latest come-from-behind win. Denver looks to stack wins this Sunday.

The Broncos pulled off another come from behind win, which was amazing for Bronco fans, but terrible for our collective blood pressure. After a poor first half, in which the team was down 16, the Broncos roared back to tie the game at 16. Coming into the game the Broncos were 5-95-1 all-time when trailing by 15 or more at the half. So now the Broncos are 6-95-1.

articles.title: More from Bayern Munich exec Karl-Heinz Rummenigge on Max Eberl contract vote abstention
articles.summary: Trouble in the FC Bayern board room?
articles.body:
Bayern Munich executive board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge admitted to abstaining from the recent vote to approve board member for sport Max Eberl's contract extension and further elaborated on the reasons why.

According to Rummenigge, his issues appear more down to process than qualms about Eberl himself. His comments were captured by Az journalist Maximilian Koch, via @iMiaSanMia .

"Something about the discussion surrounding Max irritated me," Hoeneß shared. "The impression was created that the presidential Committee had already decided on the contract extension and had merely passed that decision on to the other four members of the Supervisory Board. But that's not how it works.

"The presidential Committee can make a recommendation — but the decision is made by the entire Supervisory Board. That's exactly what irritated me the most. The presidential Committee consists of five people: Uli Hoeneß, Herbert Hainer and representatives of our three shareholders, Adidas, Audi and Allianz. If something is discussed internally and subsequently presented as nothing more than a recommendation, I have no problem with that.

"But if such a recommendation is leaked to the newspapers and creates the impression that the decision has effectively already been made, then I do have a problem with that. I make no secret of that."

Asked if he was 'personally disappointed' with Hoeneß and club president Herbert Hainer, Rummenigge did not provide a straight answer.

"I don't know who made that decision," the former Bayern CEO replied. "I only know one thing: The way it was made public was not right. I told those involved that as well — I'm a person who believes in being open and straightforward."

Bayern is moving forward with Eberl and attempting to put a show of unity and stability behind it. But reports of internal dissent have persisted , and Rummenigge's airing of his annoyances will likely not put a stop to the matter.

articles.title: Eddie Hearn disappointed with Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua press conference
articles.summary: Eddie Hearn doesn't like how the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua press conference played out.
articles.body:
Eddie Hearn wasn't impressed with how the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua press conference played out.

Fury and Joshua came together to promote their blockbuster fight scheduled for December 11. Many expected a heated exchange and promises of big performances now that the bout has been finalized , but that wasn't what we got. A more methodical approach from both men, with Fury much more composed than his usual self and Joshua in an upbeat, respectful mood. But the talking point of the presser was not either of the fighters; it was Max Kellerman.

Kellerman, the American sports personality, took center stage and hosted the press conference between the two British titans. Aside from the fighters, Kellerman took the majority of the spotlight, spending much time on the mic trying to build hype for the matchup . But Eddie Hearn didn't approve of his approach.

"I have to be honest. And I don't mean to be disrespectful to Max Kellerman, who I think is a fantastic broadcaster; they should just let me do it. Like, it's too- it's a little bit too long-winded, you know? And it's a little bit too staged, if I'm honest," Hearn stated.

Hearn expected the spotlight to be on the fighters, asking them questions and allowing them to talk between themselves to build anticipation.

Believing he does a better job, Hearn tasked fans with watching his press conference tomorrow. He will host for this weekend's battle between Ben Whittaker and Conor Wallace.

"Watch the press conference tomorrow with Ben Whittaker and Conor Wallace that I'll host," Hearn added. "I just feel like- listen. I mean this even when I talk about Jamie Ward, who is another tremendous broadcaster. And I think he's a great compare. It's just not the same. You've got to let the promoters do the press conference. Or the ones that are willing to stand up there and get things bubbling and going."

"Sometimes it can be a little bit too corporate. But I thought it was good. Quite respectful."

articles.title: Spire Responds to Joe Gibbs Racing in Latest Lawsuit Twist
articles.summary: Spire Motorsports fires back at Joe Gibbs Racing in latest lawsuit development.
articles.body:
Spire Motorsports and Chris Gabehart have responded to a motion by Joe Gibbs Racing to hold the two parties in contempt of court. It is one of the latest developments in the ongoing lawsuit between JGR against Spire and Gabehart.

The parties will meet in court on Thursday morning, with Spire and Gabehart set to explain why they should not be held in contempt of court, per Matt Weaver of Motorsport.com .

Latest Twist in The Spire, JGR NASCAR Lawsuit

When JGR first brought the case to court, the organization claimed Gabehart had stolen confidential information from the team and took it to Spire Motorsports after leaving the former at the end of the 2025 season.

JGR, which referred to the information as the "crown jewels" of the team, has filed a claim of contempt of court, accusing Gabehart of violating work restrictions at Spire Motorsports since his departure from JGR.

In a response from the Gabehart camp, the former crew chief and director of competition at JGR claims he has not gone against the court's orders.

"Every one of these witnesses, under oath, confirmed that Mr. Gabehart is not providing services of the type he provided to JGR. He has not: served as a crew chief; acted as a competition director; shared JGR's aerodynamic information; shared setup documents; communicated with GM Motorsports or Hendrick Motorsports about Cup Series; used any database for Cup purposes; been involved in any simulation, pre-event strategy, build sheets, QC materials, scans, fuel analysis, debrief forms, or project lists for Cup Series."

Gabehart currently works at Spire Motorsports as the team's chief motorsports officer. In Gabehart's short time with the organization, his legal team claims JGR's accusations of any wrongdoing are baseless.

"JGR originally sought extraordinary relief on the theory that Gabehart had taken and distributed JGR's race-car setups to Spire. It called those setups its 'crown jewels.' But extensive discovery—including more than 80 third-party subpoenas, hundreds of search terms, and searches across dozens of custodians—has not supported that theory. Spire never hired Gabehart as Competition Director or Crew Chief and never acquired JGR's trade secrets."

Chris Gabehart is a former crew chief at JGR, once atop the pit box for Denny Hamlin's No. 11 Toyota. Last year, Gabehart hung up his crew chief duties and became a director of competition for the organization.

Ahead of the 2026 season, Gabehart left JGR and joined Spire Motorsports as a chief motorsports officer. In that time period between teams, JGR claimed that Gabehart stole important information.

JGR's claim is that Gabehart stole the "crown jewels" of the team to help improve Spire Motorsports' performance.

In 2026, JGR has all four of its full-time Cup Series cars in the Chase, while Spire has two full-time drivers in the Chase — the first time the team has made the 16-driver cut in history.

articles.title: Extra Point Team of the Week, Week Five: Elba Tigers
articles.summary: ELBA, Ala. (WDHN)—After pulling off what some might call a massive upset, the Elba Tigers have claimed the latest Team of the Week honors for week five of Wi...
articles.body:
ELBA, Ala. ( WDHN )—After pulling off what some might call a massive upset, the Elba Tigers have claimed the latest Team of the Week honors for week five of Wiregrass Football.

Elba is coming off a matchup against the G.W. Long Rebels, a team they haven't defeated since 2015, in a matchup that came down to the wire as the Tigers opted to go for the game-sealing two-point conversion to capture the 37-36 victory.

With the win, the Elba Tigers now sit at 5-1 this year, continuing their five-game winning streak.

Elba will put that streak to the test this Friday, when they face off against the Pleasant Home Eagles.

articles.title: H.S. Football Notebook | Area football teams push for playoff contention
articles.summary: Fisher Catholic and Bloom-Carroll hold playoff spots as Fairfield Union fights to join the postseason race.
articles.body:
Lancaster High School's 2026 Homecoming queen announced

LANCASTER – Only three area teams – Fisher Catholic, Bloom-Carroll, and Fairfield Union - look to be in the running for the postseason. However, all three of those teams need to keep winning to keep their hopes alive.

If the playoffs began today, Fisher Catholic and Bloom-Carroll would both be in. The Irish are No. 8 in their region, while the Bulldogs stand at No. 12. The Falcons are No. 14, just on the outside looking in. They are travelling to Circleville for a huge game on Friday, Oct. 2. Both teams stand at 4-2 overall. A win by Fairfield Union should vault them into the top 12 of the computer rankings. The top 12 teams in each region qualify for the playoffs.

Fisher Catholic showed what it was made of during its 41-28 win over Miller last week. Leading 19-14 at halftime, disaster struck when the Irish turned it over on their first two offensive possessions to start the second half, and just like that, they found themselves trailing 28-19.

With time running out and things looking grim, Fisher Catholic didn't panic midway through the fourth quarter. Instead, the Irish attacked. The comeback started when Fisher Catholic was pinned back on its own 6-yard line with just nine minutes remaining. On first down, instead of playing it safe and running the ball, the Irish passed. Junior quarterback James Wilkinson connected with Damian Neal on a 94-yard touchdown pass. Wilkinson threw a perfect pass about 40 yards in the air and hit Neal in stride to cut the deficit to 28-26

After the defense got a stop, senior running back Sam Tencza raced 70 yards for a touchdown to give the lead for good, and three minutes later, Ethan O'Rielley sealed it with a 52-yard touchdown jaunt.

Fisher Catholic improved to 5-1 overall and 3-0 in the Mid-State League-Cardinal Division. The Irish will host Millersport on Oct. 2 at Fulton Field.

articles.title: OU football coach Brent Venables stands by John Mateer: 'John's our starting quarterback'
articles.summary: OU football coach Brent Venables says John Mateer remains the starting quarterback ahead of the Red River Rivalry against Texas.
articles.body:
NORMAN — OU football coach Brent Venables is standing by quarterback John Mateer for now.

After Venables said backups Whitt Newbauer and Bowe Bentley took "a lot" of reps during Wednesday's practice, he was asked if either of them will play against Texas in the Red River Rivalry next weekend.

"I have no idea," Venables said. "We're not there right now. John's our starting quarterback."

Venables said he has liked how Mateer has responded during the bye week after turning the ball over three times in the first half of the Sooners' road loss to Georgia last weekend, a game in which the coaches weighed benching Mateer.

With Mateer seemingly moving on as OU's starter, the coaching staff will need to look for ways to build back up his confidence, which Venables admitted last Saturday isn't "sky high" at the moment.

"How he responds — all of those things have been really good," Venables said. "Probably a lot better than you or I, or any of us could ever to be honest."

Oklahoma Sooners vs Georgia Bulldogs in Week 4 college football, see top photos

As for Newbauer and Bentley — listed as "ORs" on the depth chart — Venables is pleased with the progress he's seen them make. Mateer and Newbauer have mostly split the majority of the snaps this season with Bentley getting around 20% of them daily, Venables said.

Venables said each has their strength and weaknesses but pointed to their lack of experience in games.

Furthermore, Venables shared his thoughts on why most schools lack established backup quarterback in this day and age in college football.

"The money, the opportunity to go somewhere and play to make money," Venables said. "And then a school willing to to pay for two really expensive quarterbacks is another layer to it. But somebody willing to go somewhere and maybe not be the guy, guaranteed, right away. It's a little harder than you want it to be."

Bye weeks are a time for reflection and reevaluation. The Sooners' coaches have undergone extensive reevaluations of every aspect of the program this week during a disappointing season thus far.

For now, Venables is hitching his wagon to Mateer. That could always change but he's liked the response from the entire offensive unit this week as they prepare to face the Longhorns next weekend.

"We want to be a more consistent unit, obviously," Venables said. "That side of the ball has had to work a little harder, and sometimes it feels like we're going upstream. Things have been a little choppier than you want them to be. Good play, negative play. First down, have a delay. First down, tackle for loss. We want to be able to play in a better rhythm that comes from a lot of different things.

"It's a lot of little things. ... We've got to do a better job overall of executing more consistently."

articles.title: Michael King’s Gem Sets Up Padres for Deep Postseason Run
articles.summary: The San Diego Padres entered the postseason feeling very much like the underdog. That is no longer the case. They announced themselves to the world by thrash...
articles.body:
The San Diego Padres entered the postseason feeling very much like the underdog. That is no longer the case. They announced themselves to the world by thrashing the Chicago Cubs in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card Series. The offense tagged Chicago's pitchers for eight runs, with ace Michael King taking a no-hitter into the seventh inning. How might that dominance set up San Diego for a potential World Series run?

Michael King 's Strong Outing Improves Padres' Postseason Outlook

The big question mark on the Padres' roster is how far their starting rotation can take them. Behind King , the group gets thin fast. Sure, Nick Pivetta posted a 1.45 ERA in September, but he made only four starts after coming off the IL . There's a legitimate concern about how soon the wheels may come off. Veterans Walker Buehler and Robbie Ray have looked solid but not nearly dominant enough to protect early leads for long. Behind them is likely Randy Vásquez, who has been fantastic at times and ineffective at others.

There's no doubt that this rotation has an incredibly high ceiling. The question is if they can perform to that level or if they'll regress to the mean. It's hard to say. Ray and Vásquez won't pitch until a potential NLDS. Buehler wouldn't either unless the Friars drop Game 2 to Chicago. He seems likely to pitch a potential Game 3 or, if the Padres advance, start Game 1 of the NLDS against the Milwaukee Brewers .

That's why having King as a legitimate ace at the head of this rotation is so important. He showed exactly what he's capable of on Tuesday night, striking out eight batters over seven scoreless innings. He had a no-hitter going through 6 1/3 before Manny Machado misplayed a hard liner to the third-base side. Still, King did something incredible: he saved the Padres' bullpen for Game 2.

With Pivetta's relatively untested arm starting Game 2, he'll have a rather short leash given the nature of the postseason. If the righty faces trouble early, San Diego can easily turn to their relievers to finish out the game. They can ride that group to a win and give them two days' rest with a series sweep on Wednesday night. That is a veritable gold mine for the Friars in the playoffs.

It's easy to think that the Padres' bullpen is propped up by elite relievers like Mason Miller and Adrian Morejon , and there's a degree of truth to that. But the larger truth is that San Diego's bullpen is not only the best in the postseason, it's the deepest. There's high-leverage relievers galore. Beyond their two stars, the Friars have Jason Adam , Yuki Matsui , David Morgan, and Bradgley Rodriguez to turn to on their Wild Card roster . The Padres don't just have one ace in the hole; they have several.

Matsui may not look it, but he's been one of the best southpaw relievers in the game this season. He owns a 1.83 ERA with 68 strikeouts in 64 innings pitched. Despite missing an abundance of time to injury this season, Adam posted a 2.62 ERA with a 2.45 career ERA in the playoffs. Morgan posted a 2.92 ERA down the stretch with a 1.17 mark in his final seven appearances. And Rodriguez made a case for being the best rookie reliever in the league with a 2.19 ERA across 74 innings pitched.

If the Padres are to make a deep run in the playoffs, it will be on the backs of their offense and bullpen. The lineup is too potent to ignore, and the 'pen has been nails all year. By Wins Above Replacement, the Friars easily clear as the best bullpen in the postseason, totaling 8.9 WAR this season. Whether that success continues will depend on their relievers getting adequate rest. With the postseason having plenty of off days, that should bode well for San Diego.

articles.title: Michigan State basketball lands commitment from 4-star center
articles.summary: Michigan State picked up another huge recruiting win on Wednesday night
articles.body:
As we have covered these past few years, it feels like Tom Izzo has really started to figure out how to recruit in the new era of college sports, and he's put together several strong classes in a row. It looks like the 2027 class will be a continuation of that trend, as the Spartans landed their second 4-star commitment of that class on Wednesday night, as 4-star center Jaydn Jenkins committed to the Spartans.

Jenkins is the second high-profile recruit to join the Spartans in September, as they also landed a commitment from Antonio Pemberton this month.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers offers key advice ahead of Steelers’ Thursday night clash with Browns
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers wants the Steelers to build on their offensive breakthrough as Pittsburgh faces the Browns Thursday night in a key AFC North matchup.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers believes the Steelers have started to find some offensive rhythm after a difficult opening two weeks this season. Pittsburgh scored 30 points against Cincinnati on Sunday, giving the unit its first 30-point outing of the 2026 season. Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns in the 30-27 win, while Jaylen Warren added 176 total yards.

The turnaround now sends Pittsburgh to Cleveland for a Thursday night AFC North meeting. Both teams enter Week 4 at 2-1 after victories last weekend. Rodgers' message has centered on building from the Cincinnati performance without assuming the offense has arrived.

Rodgers wants Pittsburgh to build on its breakthrough

Rodgers described the Cincinnati performance as a starting point rather than a finished product. The veteran quarterback said the Steelers still have room to grow, but he also noted that positive momentum can develop when an offense puts together strong performances in succession.

" We're gonna try and stack a few ," Rodgers said, according to NFL.com. The comment captures the central challenge for Pittsburgh on a short week: turn one productive afternoon into a more consistent offensive identity.

The Steelers entered Week 3 after scoring only 23 points combined in their first two games, a 20-13 win over Atlanta and a 20-3 loss to New England . Their 30-point showing against Cincinnati changed the immediate conversation because Rodgers connected on two deep touchdown passes in the first quarter after failing to complete a deep throw on his first nine attempts of the season.

Cincinnati showed what the offense can become

Rodgers finished the Cincinnati game with 292 passing yards and three touchdowns, producing his strongest statistical outing of the season. Warren also broke loose for 127 rushing yards on 17 carries and added 49 receiving yards, giving Pittsburgh a productive balance between its passing and rushing attack.

Darnell Washington supplied another major play with a 47-yard reception from Rodgers. The Steelers used explosive plays early, then continued moving the ball efficiently as the game developed, a contrast to the stalled possessions that defined much of the first two weeks.

The performance also came under the new head coach, Mike McCarthy, and a revamped offensive structure. Rodgers has acknowledged that the group is still learning how to operate together, making the Cincinnati game an important reference point without establishing a long-term trend on its own.

The Browns present a different defensive test

Cleveland enters Thursday night with a 2-1 record after winning consecutive games against Tampa Bay and Carolina. The Browns followed a 34-10 season-opening loss to Jacksonville with a 23-19 victory over Tampa Bay and a 21-18 win over Carolina.

NFL.com noted that Cleveland's defense has played especially well during the two-game winning streak. That creates a different challenge for Rodgers after Cincinnati allowed Pittsburgh to generate explosive plays and 30 points.

The matchup also carries AFC North significance, as both teams are 2-1. The winner will move to 3-1 and claim an early advantage in the division standings, while the losing team will fall to .500 after four games in the AFC North race.

Pittsburgh has another short week to manage

Thursday games compress preparation and recovery, and Steelers players have openly discussed the difficulty of the schedule. Cameron Heyward said communication and rest are especially important during the abbreviated week, while safety Jaquan Brisker emphasized arriving fresh and prepared.

Rodgers' experience gives him a long history of playing on short weeks, but Pittsburgh's broader challenge involves an offense that is still developing under McCarthy. The team adjusted its weekly schedule to give players additional recovery time, with Tuesday's practice pushed later in the day.

The short turnaround also limits the amount of new material teams can install. Pittsburgh linebacker Patrick Queen said the division matchup will come down to execution across offense, defense, and special teams rather than a large volume of new concepts.

The Cleveland setting adds another layer

The Steelers have lost their last four games in Cleveland, dating to a 29-17 Browns victory in September 2022. Pittsburgh did win the next meeting at home that season, but the recent road results remain part of the matchup's context.

Rodgers also faced Cleveland's defense during his first season with Pittsburgh. In the December 2025 meeting at Huntington Bank Field, the Browns held the Steelers to six points in a 13-6 victory, with Rodgers completing 21 of 39 passes for 168 yards.

The venue has therefore been a difficult setting for Pittsburgh in recent seasons. Cleveland's defense has repeatedly made it challenging for the Steelers to sustain offense there, adding another layer to Rodgers' latest road matchup with the Browns.

Fun fact: Aaron Rodgers once completed 23 straight passes against USC, tying the NCAA single-game record at the time. The streak helped him finish 23-for-26 in the game and extend his overall streak to 26 consecutive completions.

Rodgers' message fits the Steelers' current situation

The quarterback's emphasis on stacking performances is particularly relevant because Pittsburgh's season has already swung between two very different offensive showings. The Steelers opened with a 20-13 win over Atlanta, struggled in a 20-3 loss to New England, then responded with a win over Cincinnati.

Rodgers has 700 passing yards, four touchdowns, and two interceptions through three games in 2026. His 58.4 completion percentage and 81.0 passer rating show that the offense still has statistical room to improve even after the Cincinnati breakthrough.

The Browns will test whether Pittsburgh can maintain the aggressive passing approach while handling a defense that has helped produce consecutive wins. Cleveland's own offense has also improved across its two-game winning streak, creating a matchup between two 2-1 AFC North teams with different paths to the same early position.

Aaron Rodgers wants Pittsburgh to build on its 30-point performance against Cincinnati.

Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns in the Week 3 win.

Jaylen Warren produced 127 rushing yards and 49 receiving yards against Cincinnati.

The Steelers and Browns both enter Thursday night at 2-1.

Cleveland has won two straight games after opening the season with a loss.

Pittsburgh has lost its last four road games against Cleveland.

Rodgers has emphasized consistency as the Steelers prepare for another AFC North matchup.

articles.title: 49ers practice squad signees Matthew Judon, Dante Pettis could play Sunday
articles.summary: Two recent San Francisco 49ers signees, edge rusher Matthew Judon and wide receiver Dante Pettis, fill areas of need and could play Sunday against the Bronco...
articles.body:
Another week, another round of reinforcements for the San Francisco 49ers .

Neither player appeared during the open locker room period, but new practice squad signees Matthew Judon (No. 43) and Dante Pettis (No. 15) already had their lockers in place on Wednesday. And both players took to the practice field.

Pettis, a receiver, and Judon, an edge rusher, worked in with their respective units during position drills, two spots that have been decimated by injuries. So decimated, in fact, that Pettis and Judon have non-zero chances to be active on Sunday against the Denver Broncos .

Niners fans will surely remember Pettis, a former second-round pick who spent the first 2½ years of his career with the franchise before being waived in 2020. His first stint did not work out well, of course, but head coach Kyle Shanahan said he was "pumped" that Pettis remained available on the free agent market. Shanahan did not appear to be a huge fan of Pettis' abilities during his first stint with the team, yet he downplayed any prior issues on Wednesday.

Asked about how they left things, Shanahan said: "Fine. There was no relationship issue. That was just how it worked out. People get confused sometimes with saying people are in the doghouse. … People sometimes get that confused with just coaching. But I've always loved Dante. Dante's a great dude. He's got a lot of abilities, done some great things since we let him go other places."

In fact, Shanahan added, San Francisco attempted to sign Pettis during this year's training camp as they dealt with a handful of wide receiver injuries.

"Tried it again this time," Shanahan said, "and this time it worked out."

If Mike Evans (ribs) - who did not practice Wednesday - misses Sunday's game against the Broncos, there is still no guarantee Pettis reaches the active roster. He would need to supplant one of these five receivers to be active on game day: Deebo Samuel , Jordan Watkins , Jacob Cowing , KhaDarel Hodge and, likely, Brandin Cooks , who remains on the practice squad but figures to have a strong chance to suit up eventually. Worth noting: Hodge missed Wednesday's practice with a knee injury, so that could bode well for Pettis' chances of being up.

"A fellow 2018er!" linebacker Fred Warner said of Pettis, referring to the year both players got drafted. "It was getting lonely. … Great to have him back. Good buddy of mine. Fits right in."

Another 49ers' defensive lineman popped up on the injury report Wednesday in Keion White (hamstring). Following injuries to Nick Bosa (calf) and practically everyone else at the position, White suddenly became San Francisco's most vital edge rusher. He played 56 snaps on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals , followed by 51 for Khalid Kareem , 47 for Ogbo Okoronkwo and 13 for Villami Fehoko. The good news for the 49ers: Although he did not practice, White did some light exercise on a side field during Wednesday's open viewing portion. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw , who suffered a quad injury Sunday, did the same. Neither injury appears too serious.

Not on the practice field Wednesday, in addition to Bosa and Hodge: T Trent Williams (neck), Evans (ribs), RB Christian McCaffrey (rest) and DT James Thompson Jr. (ankle). Defensive ends Romello Height (hand) and Mykel Williams (knee) returned to the practice field in limited capacity. Height missed all of last week after breaking his hand against the Miami Dolphins , while Williams had his 21-day practice window opened after beginning the season on the physically unable to perform list.
